summary: This text pretends to be T-Mobile and pushes you to a fake website with a deadline.

findings.title: First-time sender, long code
findings.explanation: Real T-Mobile alerts come from short codes, not a 10-digit number you have never texted.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: If this came from 611 or a known T-Mobile short code, I would trust it more.

findings.title: Lookalike domain
findings.explanation: 't-mobi1e' uses a number 1 instead of the letter l. The site was registered 3 days ago.

findings.title: Deadline pressure
findings.explanation: 'Suspended in 2 hrs' is meant to make you act before you think.

findings.title: Pretends to be T-Mobile
findings.explanation: The brand name appears but the sender and link are not T-Mobile's. Call the real T-Mobile: 611.
